# Configure external credential injection

This page describes how to configure a terminating gateway on Kubernetes to inject a credential into approved external HTTP calls. To learn how credential injection works, refer to [External credential injection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/credential-injection).

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Requirements

- Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric installed with `ai.enabled` set to `true` and credential injection enabled on a terminating gateway. Refer to [Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/install).

## Choose a credential source

The [`terminatingGateways.defaults.credentialInjection.source`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-terminatinggateways-defaults-credentialinjection-source) Helm value selects how credentials reach the Credential Injection Processor.

| Source | How credentials arrive |
| --- | --- |
| `vault` | Default. A Vault Agent sidecar authenticates to Vault with the gateway's Kubernetes service account and renders each credential to a memory-backed volume that only the Credential Injection Processor reads. |
| `kubernetesSecret` | Consul mounts the Kubernetes Secret named in `secretName` read-only into the Credential Injection Processor. Each data key in the Secret is a credential file for one binding. |

Kubernetes Secrets are a weaker posture than Vault. They are base64-encoded at rest and readable through the Kubernetes API by anyone with RBAC access. Enable etcd encryption at rest and scope RBAC before you use the `kubernetesSecret` source.

## Configure the gateway deployment

Set the credential injection Helm values for the terminating gateway. The processor and Vault Agent read their configuration from ConfigMaps that you create in the gateway's namespace.

<CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

```yaml
terminatingGateways:
  enabled: true
  defaults:
    credentialInjection:
      enabled: true
      source: vault
      processorImage: "<credential-injection-image>"
      vaultAgentImage: "<vault-agent-image>"
      processorConfigMap: "<processor-configmap-name>"
      vaultAgentConfigMap: "<vault-agent-configmap-name>"
      vaultAddress: "<vault-address>"
      vaultCAConfigMap: "<vault-ca-configmap-name>"
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

<!-- TODO: Document the contents of the processor and Vault Agent ConfigMaps, including how a binding ID maps to a Vault secret path. Source is not available in consul-k8s v2.1.0. -->

For every setting, refer to [`terminatingGateways.defaults.credentialInjection`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-terminatinggateways-defaults-credentialinjection) in the Helm chart reference.

## Store the credential

Store each binding's credential in Vault as a KV secret. For the required fields and the rotation rules, refer to [Credential delivery](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/credential-injection#credential-delivery).

## Configure the terminating gateway routes

Link each external service to the terminating gateway and set its credential policy.

1. Enable credential injection routing in the terminating gateway configuration. The Credential Injection Processor socket in a Kubernetes credential injection pod is `/consul/auth-socket/auth.sock`, which is the default.
1. Set `credential.mode` on every linked service. Set `inject` to add a credential, or `none` to forward requests without one.
1. For each service in `inject` mode, set a unique `bindingID`, a `caFile`, and a DNS name in `sni`. Consul rejects the configuration without them, so a credential is never sent over plaintext.

<CodeBlockConfig filename="terminating-gateway.yaml">

```yaml
apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
kind: TerminatingGateway
metadata:
  name: terminating-gateway
spec:
  credentialInjection:
    udsPath: /consul/auth-socket/auth.sock
  services:
    - name: external-mcp
      caFile: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
      sni: mcp.example.com
      credential:
        mode: inject
        bindingID: external-mcp
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

Wildcard service names are not supported when you enable credential injection. For every field, refer to the [terminating gateway configuration entry reference](/consul/docs/reference/config-entry/terminating-gateway).

Apply the resource:

```shell-session
$ kubectl apply --filename terminating-gateway.yaml
```

## Monitor credential health

The Credential Injection Processor logs a `credential_reload` event for each binding with the accepted `kv_version` and an outcome. It also periodically logs a `credential_status` event that reports whether each binding is usable. For details, refer to [Readiness and rotation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/credential-injection#readiness-and-rotation).
